title: A density gradient centrifugation method for rapid separation of nanoTiO2 and TiO2 aggregates from microalgal cells in complex mixtures with mercury
author: Li, Slaveykova

steps.title: Prepare nanoTiO2 stock solution
steps.instruction: Disperse nanoTiO2 in ultrapure water to a concentration of 2.0 g L⁻¹ and sonicate for 10 min at 50 W L⁻¹, 40 kHz; repeat an additional 10 min sonication immediately before dosing.

steps.title: Clean and autoclave glassware
steps.instruction: Soak all glassware for at least 24 h in 5 % v/v HNO₃, rinse three times with ultrapure water, then autoclave before use.

steps.title: Prepare sucrose gradient solutions
steps.instruction: Make w/v sucrose solutions of 20 %–60 % (for algal localization testing), 20 %–100 % (for nanoTiO₂ testing), and the final working concentrations of 40 % w/v (for separating dispersed nanoTiO₂ from algae) and 100 % w/v (for separating compact TiO₂ aggregates from algae).

steps.title: Optimize sucrose concentrations (optional)
steps.instruction: Test algal localization in 20 %–60 % sucrose (nanoTiO₂‑free medium) and nanoTiO₂ localization in 20 %–100 % sucrose (alga‑free medium) to confirm buoyant densities; keep the total separation time as short as possible (3–5 min) and evaluate temperatures of 4 °C and 20 °C.

steps.title: Conduct density gradient centrifugation
steps.instruction: Layer the exposure mixture onto the appropriate sucrose solution (40 % w/v for dispersed nanoTiO₂, 100 % w/v for aggregates) and centrifuge for 4 min at 1600 g, 4 °C. The upper 100 % sucrose layer will appear green, indicating the algal cell band.

steps.title: Collect algal layer and resuspend
steps.instruction: Carefully aspirate the green‑colored band from the 100 % sucrose layer, resuspend it in the same volume as the original algal suspension, and keep the fraction for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Quantify cellular mercury by AMA 254
steps.instruction: Measure Hg content in the algal fraction before and after separation using atomic absorption spectrometry with the Advanced Hg Analyzer AMA 254 (Altec s.r.l., Czech Republic).

steps.title: Validate separation using flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Analyze pre‑ and post‑centrifugation samples on a BD Accuri C6 flow cytometer (software 264.15) equipped with a 488 nm argon laser and FL3 (>670 nm) detector. Set the primary threshold to 20 000 events on FSC‑H. Use the following gating sequence: (1) FSC‑H vs FSC‑A dot‑plot to remove doublets/background; (2) SSC‑A vs FSC‑A and count vs FL3 plots to discriminate algae (high chlorophyll autofluorescence) from TiO₂ aggregates (size/granularity differences). Record cell densities and aggregate counts for recovery calculations.

substeps.instruction: Set laser and detector parameters (488 nm excitation, FL3 >670 nm).
Apply primary threshold of 20 000 on FSC‑H.
Gate SSC‑A/FSC‑A and count/FL3 to separate algae from TiO₂ aggregates.
Measure cell concentration (initially ~1.0 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹) and TiO₂ concentrations (2–200 mg L⁻¹).

description: To evaluate the efficiency of the separation of the microalgae from the aggregates of nanoTiO2, the cell numbers and the numbers of TiO2 aggregates were determined by using flow cytometry before and after density gradient centrifugation. 488 nm argon excitation laser and fluorescence detection channel with band pass emission filters at a long pass emission filter for > 670 nm (FL3) were used. Data acquisition and analysis were performed with the BD Accuri C6 Software 264.15. The primary threshold was set to 20,000 events on FSC-H. Algal cells were discriminated from nanoTiO2 aggregates applying the gating strategy shown on Fig. 4. The log FSC-H versus log FSC-A dot-plot was used first to remove cell doublets or artefacts. Then two different plots (log SSC-A versus log FSC-A and count versus log FL3) were used to distinguish algal cells and TiO2 aggregates based on the difference in their size and chlorophyll autofluorescence specific for alga.Fig. 4Schematic representation of the FCM data analysis procedure used to define the gate corresponding to algae and nanoTiO2 aggregates. As a first step FSC-H/FSC-A dot-plot (A) was used to remove eventual instrument background. Then signals present in the gated region were plotted in a count versus red fluorescence plot (B) and SSC/FSC dot-plot (C) to verify cellular characteristics of size, granularity and chlorophyll autofluorescence. (D) cytogram of algal suspension (1.0 × 106 cells/mL) in the absence of nanoTiO2, (E) cytogram of 200 mg L−1 nanoTiO2 suspension only (F) cytogram of mixture containing 1.0 × 106 cells/mL algaeand 200 mg L−1 nanoTiO2.Fig. 4 After density gradient centrifugation, the fractions collected from the region containing the green colored bands were resuspended in the same volume of initial algal suspensions and the cell densities were measured by FCM.
